newsitem.title: GERMANY: German import prices at nearly six yr high.
newsitem.headline: German import prices at nearly six yr high.

text.p: German import prices in February hit their highest levels since the middle of 1991, spurred on by a strong dollar and prices of raw materials and oil, the Federal Statistics Office said on Tuesday.
Import prices rose 0.5 percent in February from the previous month for a year-on-year increase of 3.0 percent. The index was 100.5 compared to 100.0 in January and 97.6 a year ago.
Import prices rose 1.0 percent in January from the month before and were up 2.6 percent year-on-year.

The last time import prices -- an indication of inflation trends -- were at February's levels was in June 1991, when the annual change showed a rise of 3.5 percent, and in July 1991, when import prices rose 3.3 percent from the year earlier.
But since then, the statistics office said, import prices had been continually declining until the recent rise of the dollar against the mark.
"There could also be other reasons behind it, but the dollar exchange rate is playing a considerable role, as well as oil prices and raw materials," a statistics office official told Reuters.
Excluding oil and petroleum products, the import prices index rose 0.9 percent in February from January and was up 1.4 percent from February a year ago.
The statistics office said the raw materials index rose 24 percent year-on-year in February, while finished manufacturing goods prices were up just 0.5 percent.
Export prices in February rose 0.3 percent from January and were up 0.8 percent from the same month a year earlier.
